newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil government authorizes telecom rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Brazil government authorizes telecom rate rise.

text.p: The Brazilian government will introduce Friday new tariffs for the telecommunications sector, the communications ministry said.
The average increase for subscribers would be 8.3 percent, the ministry said in a statement.
The increase would lead to a net increase of 3.1 percent in revenues for telecom operators in Brazil.

The ministry said the rate increase represents the second and final stage of a restructuring of tariffs in the telecommunications sector. The first increase took place between November 1995 and February 1996.
The new increase was aimed at setting tariffs that reflect the cost of services, reducing existing cross subsidies between services and setting "fairer" rates for the varying services.
In its statement the ministry said tariffs for public telephone services, which account for 74.9 percent of receipts, would be increased 8.29 percent.
Cellular rates, accounting for 15.46 percent of income, would be cut by one percent, while data transfers, seven percent of income, would be reduced 41.85 percent.
The ministry was also establishing a fixed 300-real charge for installation of new telephones over the medium term.

The rates for domestic long distance calls would be cut by 32 percent. International calls within the Mercosur customs union would be reduced by 10 percent; to the United States by 30 percent; Europe by 13 percent; Japan by 15 percent and to other countries by five percent.

The one-percent cut in cellular charges has already been put into effect in a reduction in December 1996. The cuts in international data transfer, telephone pulses and public pay phones will take effect April 4. The 300-real installation charge will take effect May 1 and long distance domestic calls and subscriber charges will be cut from May 19.
